name: Steve Rogers

summary: Steve Rogers was born in New York City in 1922 and grew up thin and sickly through the Great Depression. His father died while he was a boy and his mother was lost to pneumonia in his late teens, but both left him with a stubborn sense of duty. He studied art, and when newsreels showed fascist armies tearing through Europe and Asia he tried to enlist, only to be turned away as unfit. General Chester Phillips overheard how badly he wanted to serve and offered him a place in a secret programme called Operation Rebirth.

In a hidden Washington laboratory, Dr. Abraham Erskine, working under the cover name Professor Reinstein, gave Steve the Super-Soldier Serum and then flooded him with vita-rays. He walked out of the chamber at the very peak of human ability. Minutes later a Nazi spy shot Erskine dead, and because the scientist had never fully written down his formula, Steve remained its only success. After months of intensive training he was given a star-spangled costume as America's answer to the Red Skull, plus a cover identity as a clumsy private at Camp Lehigh, where the camp mascot Bucky Barnes stumbled on his secret and became his partner.

Through the war Captain America fought alongside Bucky and the Invaders, and President Roosevelt later presented him with the round shield that became his signature. In the closing days of the conflict the pair tried to stop a drone plane packed with explosives launched by Baron Zemo. The blast seemed to kill Bucky and hurled Steve into icy Arctic waters, where the serum preserved him in suspended animation. Decades later the Sub-Mariner found the frozen figure being worshipped by an Inuit tribe and flung it into the sea, and the newly formed Avengers pulled it out and revived him.

comics.title: Meet Captain America
comics.summary: Captain America arrives fully formed in his first issue, with his super-soldier origin, his teenage partner Bucky and a sinister Red Skull all introduced in one go. Its cover, which went on sale in December 1940, famously shows him knocking Hitler flat. The origin was later expanded and reconciled in Silver Age retellings, including Captain America #109 and #255.

comics.title: Man out of time
comics.summary: Thawed out by the Avengers, Steve joins as the team's first new recruit and is later treated as an honorary founder. He clashes with his wartime enemy Baron Zemo and his Masters of Evil while still grieving the partner he believes he lost. When the founders step away, he takes command of a scrappy new lineup of Hawkeye, Quicksilver and the Scarlet Witch, later nicknamed Cap's Kooky Quartet.

comics.title: Nomad
comics.summary: Investigating the Secret Empire, Steve discovers its leader is a senior figure in the US government, and the cover-up that follows shakes his faith in the flag he wears. He gives up the shield and becomes Nomad, a hero with no country. When a young admirer who took up the role is murdered by the Red Skull, Steve returns as Captain America, now standing for the nation's ideals rather than its officials.

comics.title: Battleworld and the mansion siege
comics.summary: Steve is among the heroes the Beyonder snatches away to fight on Battleworld in the original Secret Wars. Back home, Helmut Zemo's Masters of Evil seize Avengers Mansion, torture Jarvis in front of him and destroy irreplaceable mementos of his past, including his only photo of his mother. He ends the siege by beating Zemo in a rooftop duel.

comics.title: The Captain
comics.summary: A government commission tells Steve he was never discharged and orders him to serve as a directed operative. Unwilling to take orders blindly, he hands the shield and the name to John Walker and carries on in a new uniform as the Captain. Once the Red Skull is exposed as the hidden hand behind the commission, Walker steps aside and Steve takes the shield back.

comics.title: The Winter Soldier and Civil War
comics.summary: Steve learns that a Soviet assassin called the Winter Soldier is his old partner Bucky, brainwashed and kept on ice between missions, and he uses a Cosmic Cube to give Bucky back his memories. When the Superhuman Registration Act divides the hero community, Steve goes underground to lead the resistance against Tony Stark's side. He wins the final battle but surrenders when he sees the damage the fight is doing to the people he wants to protect.

comics.title: The Death of Captain America and Reborn
comics.summary: On the courthouse steps, a Red Skull plot ends with a sniper's bullet and shots from a brainwashed Sharon Carter, and Steve dies. In truth his mind had been cast adrift in time, reliving moments of his life, until he fights his way back into his own body. After helping topple Norman Osborn during the Siege of Asgard, he lets Bucky keep the shield and becomes America's chief of security.

comics.title: Dimension Z and passing the shield
comics.summary: Arnim Zola drags Steve into the hostile realm of Dimension Z, where he spends more than a decade raising a rescued boy named Ian as his son, only to learn that no time at all has passed on Earth. Not long after his return, the villain Iron Nail switches off the serum in his body and Steve ages rapidly to his real age of over ninety. He names Sam Wilson as the new Captain America.

comics.title: Secret Empire
comics.summary: Kobik, a living Cosmic Cube with the mind of a child, restores Steve's youth, but she has been secretly schooled by the Red Skull and rewrites history to produce a Captain America loyal to Hydra. That double seizes the United States while the real Steve survives only as a memory inside Kobik's mind. When the Cube is made whole again, the true Steve returns and defeats his fascist counterpart.

comics.title: Framed, empowered and sharing the shield
comics.summary: Framed for murder by a shadowy group, Steve is broken out of prison and declares Captain America dead, fighting on for a while under his own name. Back in the role, he is drawn into the Phoenix Force's tournament for a new host, where a Phoenix-powered Doctor Doom yields to him and the Phoenix later names him the winner of his bout with Shang-Chi. Afterwards he and Sam Wilson agree that both of them will carry the title of Captain America.

screen.title: Captain America (TV film)
screen.summary: In this CBS television film Steve is a former Marine turned travelling artist whose late father developed a strength serum called F.L.A.G. After an attempt on his life, doctors give him the serum to save him. He adopts a costume built on one of his own sketches and stops a villain who has built a neutron bomb.

screen.title: Captain America II: Death Too Soon (TV film)
screen.summary: The second CBS film sends Steve after General Miguel, a terrorist who has kidnapped a scientist and forced him to produce a chemical that speeds up ageing. Miguel tests it on a small town and then threatens a city with it. Captain America tracks down his base, the villain is caught by his own weapon, and Steve secures the antidote.

screen.title: Captain America
screen.summary: Barred from the draft because of polio, Steve volunteers for a secret super-serum project in World War II and becomes Captain America, facing an Italian-made Red Skull. He reawakens decades later in a very different 1990s America. There he discovers the Skull is still active and plotting against the President, his wartime comrade Tom Kimball.

sources.label: Marvel Fandom wiki: Captain America (1990 film)

screen.title: Captain America: The First Avenger
screen.summary: A frail Brooklyn volunteer is chosen by Abraham Erskine for Project Rebirth and emerges as a super-soldier, only to be sent out to sell war bonds on a USO stage. He goes rogue to rescue captured troops, including Bucky Barnes, then leads the Howling Commandos against Hydra and the Red Skull. To stop a bomber aimed at America he brings the Valkyrie down in the Arctic ice, waking almost seventy years later.

screen.title: The Avengers
screen.summary: Still adjusting to the modern world, Steve is recruited by Nick Fury to help recover the Tesseract from Loki. He butts heads with Tony Stark aboard the Helicarrier, but in the Battle of New York he takes tactical command and directs the team against the Chitauri invasion.

sources.label: Marvel Cinematic Universe Wiki: The Avengers

screen.title: Captain America: The Winter Soldier
screen.summary: Working as a S.H.I.E.L.D. agent, Steve uncovers that Hydra has hollowed out the agency from within and plans to use Project Insight's Helicarriers to kill millions. Branded a fugitive, he teams with Natasha Romanoff and new ally Sam Wilson. The masked assassin hunting them turns out to be Bucky, and Steve refuses to fight him as the Helicarriers fall.

screen.title: Avengers: Age of Ultron
screen.summary: Steve leads the Avengers in the raid on Hydra that recovers Loki's sceptre, then against Ultron, the rogue artificial intelligence that grows out of Tony Stark's peacekeeping plan. After the Battle of Sokovia he stays behind with Natasha to train a new Avengers lineup.

screen.title: Ant-Man
screen.summary: Cameo in the post-credits scene. Steve and Sam Wilson have finally tracked down Bucky Barnes, but the Sokovia Accords mean they cannot call Tony Stark for help. Sam says he knows someone who might do instead. Chris Evans is uncredited.

screen.title: Captain America: Civil War
screen.summary: Steve refuses to sign the Sokovia Accords and goes on the run to protect Bucky, who has been framed for a deadly bombing. The split between the Avengers explodes in a clash at a German airport. It ends in a brutal fight with Tony Stark in Siberia, after which Steve leaves his shield behind.

screen.title: Spider-Man: Homecoming
screen.summary: Cameo through archive classroom videos. Steve appears in the fitness challenge and public service films that Midtown School still plays for its students. The post-credits scene is one of these clips, a talk on patience that ends with him asking how many more he has to film.

screen.title: Avengers: Infinity War
screen.summary: Living as a fugitive since the Civil War, Steve resurfaces with Natasha and Sam to rescue Wanda Maximoff and Vision. He leads the defence of Wakanda against Thanos's armies, but cannot prevent the Snap that wipes out half of all life.

screen.title: Captain Marvel
screen.summary: Cameo in the credits scene set in 2018. Steve, Natasha, Bruce Banner and James Rhodes are studying Nick Fury's pager after the Snap when it goes dead. Carol Danvers suddenly appears and asks where Fury is. Chris Evans is uncredited.

screen.title: Avengers: Endgame
screen.summary: Five years after the Snap, Steve helps plan the Time Heist to recover the Infinity Stones, and in the final battle proves worthy of lifting Mjolnir. Afterwards he returns the Stones to their places in time, stays in the past to build a life with Peggy Carter, and as an old man hands his shield to Sam Wilson. The MCU Wiki notes that the September 2026 Encore re-release extends his scene with Peggy, which Loki interrupts at the door.

screen.title: Avengers: Endgame (Encore re-release)
screen.summary: Marvel Studios returned Endgame to theaters in September 2026. Co-director Anthony Russo told Marvel that the Encore plays one beat past the moment where Steve Rogers’ story ended with Peggy Carter, and that the moment carries a different meaning.

trivia.fact: Joe Simon briefly considered calling the character Super American before settling on Captain America, reasoning that comics had plenty of Supers but few Captains.

sources.label: Marvel Fandom wiki: Steven Rogers (Earth-616)

trivia.fact: Captain America Comics #1 went on sale on 20 December 1940 with a cover of Cap punching Hitler, an image later parodied in Captain America: The First Avenger.

sources.label: Marvel Fandom wiki: Captain America Comics Vol 1 #1

trivia.fact: His first shield was a wedge-shaped badge design; the familiar round disc arrived in his second issue.
